sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the inspector
sections.what: Brings in the icons and the citation hook. It does not show anything on screen by itself.
sections.why: Needed so the file can use shared citation data and draw icons.

sections.name: STATUS_LABEL
sections.title: Status labels
sections.what: Gives plain-English labels for each source status, such as Verified on source, Partly found on source and Source unreachable.
sections.why: Readers see what the status means instead of a code word.
sections.watch_out: A new status added on the server needs a label here, or readers will see the raw code.

sections.name: STATUS_TONE
sections.title: Status colours
sections.what: Gives each status a colour style, with green for verified or captured, gold for partly found, grey for unreachable or inaccessible, and red for unverified or unsourced.
sections.why: Lets readers spot weak sources at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Grey is used for both unreachable and inaccessible sources, so readers cannot tell a server failure from an access block.

sections.name: StatusPill
sections.title: Status badge
sections.what: Draws a small rounded label that shows the status's readable text in its colour. If the status is unknown, it uses a neutral style and shows the raw text.
sections.why: Gives every status display the same look in one component.
sections.watch_out: Unknown statuses fall back to a neutral style, which can make a new problem look ordinary.

summary: This file holds the labels, colours and small status badge used to show whether a source check passed, failed or is missing.
purpose: Lets the citation and source views show a clear status for each source check.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Keeping the status words and colours in one file keeps the badges consistent wherever they are used.
how: It defines a plain-English label for each status, a colour style for each status, and a small badge component that shows the matching label and colour. If a status is not known, it shows the raw status text with spaces in place of underscores.
inputs: A status text such as verified, partial, unreachable, unverified, unsourced, captured or inaccessible.
outputs: A small coloured badge with a readable label.
risks: A status without a label or colour falls back to a generic style, which may hide a real problem. The colours are the main signal, so a status colour that is changed could mislead readers.
debug: If a badge shows a raw code, check that the status is in the label list. If a badge looks the wrong colour, check its tone entry.
